$comment: The PUBLIC sample answer key. Committed on purpose. `pnpm gen --sample` builds src/lib/generated/sample/ from this, which is what a fresh clone plays until someone runs `pnpm gen` with a real flags.secret.json. Every sample flag ends in _sample so nobody mistakes a demo instance for a live one. Hints and writeups are deliberately empty: publishing the real ones would spoil every deployment, not just this demo.

honeypots.pctf{n1ce_try_but_no}: That one was painted on the page in twenty-four-point type. Flags that want to be found aren't flags.
honeypots.pctf{grep_is_not_a_solution}: Found in a source comment, was it? Comments are where developers put things they've stopped thinking about.
honeypots.pctf{th4ts_a_decoy_friend}: A plausible-looking string in a payload file. Plausible is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
honeypots.pctf{i_read_the_registry}: The registry holds hashes. If a readable flag appeared there, someone put it there on purpose.
